items.original_text: Filing step: Identify and secure an agreement to purchase or transfer an ABC Type 42 license from another bar located within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District. What to say: Engage an ABC license broker to find a Type 42 (or a Type 48 if available, though the concept serves only beer and wine) currently held by a bar premises inside the Mission SUD boundaries. Verify with Planning that the source address is within the SUD before entering escrow. Negotiate a contingent purchase agreement: the transfer closes only after the CUA and POE permit are approved. Budget $10,000–$50,000 for a Type 42 in San Francisco (non-quota licenses are cheaper than quota Types 47/48 but still trade at a premium in restricted districts). Do not file the ABC transfer application until the CUA is approved, because ABC will refer it to Planning and Planning will not approve the referral without the CUA in place.

items.original_text: Filing step: File the DPH health permit to operate application after the building permit is issued and kitchen construction is substantially complete. What to say: Apply online for the permit to operate at least one month before opening, providing the Business Account Number (BAN), Location ID (LIN), federal EIN, the approved building permit number, proof that a certified food safety manager is on staff (ServSafe or equivalent), and the menu. Pay the $470 application fee (includes the initial inspection); the annual license fee is $0 for bars and restaurants through 2028. DPH will schedule the pre-opening inspection; the inspector will verify that the kitchen layout matches the approved plans, all equipment is installed and operational, hand sinks and sanitizer are in place, and food handler cards are on file for all employees. The permit is issued after the final inspection passes; you cannot serve food or drink to the public before it is issued.

items.original_text: Estimated time: 287 to 735 days. Estimated government cost: $8,893 to $27,780. Notes: Time to approval: 287–735 days covers the entitlement path (Conditional Use Authorization, Place of Entertainment permit, health permit to operate, and building permit with change of use) when all are granted. The critical path is the CUA (120–300 days from filing to Commission approval plus 30-day appeal period) followed by the POE permit (45–120 days, but typically continued until after the CUA is final), then the ABC Type 42 transfer with PCN finding (90–180 days including the 1–3 month Board of Supervisors PCN process), the building permit plan review and construction inspections (14–120 days), and the DPH permit to operate (14–45 days after construction is substantially complete). The minimum assumes an uncontested CUA at 120 days, POE filed in parallel and approved 45 days after the CUA is final, ABC transfer with PCN at 90 days, building permit at 14 days, and health permit at 14 days: 120 + 30 (appeal) + 45 + 60 + 14 + 14 = 283 days; round to 287. The maximum assumes a continued CUA hearing, appeals, or conditions that extend the CUA to 300 days, POE continued and then taking 120 days after CUA finality, ABC transfer with protests and PCN delays at 180 days, building permit plan review and correction cycles at 120 days, and health permit re-inspections at 45 days: 300 + 30 + 120 + 180 + 120 + 45 = 795 days, reduced to 735 to reflect that some steps overlap (POE and ABC both wait for CUA finality but then run concurrently). This is the time to obtain the approvals; it does not include the time to identify and escrow the Type 42 license (which must happen before ABC filing), construction time after the building permit is issued, or the time to a denial or a withdrawal. Government fees (minimum): SF business registration $55, CUA application $3,100 (or $0 with first-year-free waiver), POE permit $2,708, health plan check $828, health permit to operate $470, building permit (low end) $800, ABC Type 42 transfer $1,000, plus state entity registration $70, seller's permit $0, food safety manager cert $100, RBS training (8 employees) $240, food handler cards (8 employees) $112, EDD/workers' comp $0, sign permit $300, total minimum $8,893 assuming the CUA fee waiver; without waiver add $3,100 = $11,993. Maximum: business registration $700, CUA $15,000 (if construction value is high or fees are not waived), POE $3,800, health plan check $2,500, health permit $1,000, building permit $15,000, ABC $1,600, plus entity $150, food safety $250, RBS $240, food handler $120, sign permit $1,500, total $27,780. These are government filing fees only; they do not include the cost to purchase the Type 42 license ($10,000–$50,000 estimated), attorney and consultant fees, architect and contractor costs, or the premiums for workers' compensation and liability insurance. The Type 42 license purchase is the largest single cost and must be secured before ABC filing.

Notes: Time to approval: 287–735 days covers the entitlement path (Conditional Use Authorization, Place of Entertainment permit, health permit to operate, and building permit with change of use) when all are granted. The critical path is the CUA (120–300 days from filing to Commission approval plus 30-day appeal period) followed by the POE permit (45–120 days, but typically continued until after the CUA is final), then the ABC Type 42 transfer with PCN finding (90–180 days including the 1–3 month Board of Supervisors PCN process), the building permit plan review and construction inspections (14–120 days), and the DPH permit to operate (14–45 days after construction is substantially complete). The minimum assumes an uncontested CUA at 120 days, POE filed in parallel and approved 45 days after the CUA is final, ABC transfer with PCN at 90 days, building permit at 14 days, and health permit at 14 days: 120 + 30 (appeal) + 45 + 60 + 14 + 14 = 283 days; round to 287. The maximum assumes a continued CUA hearing, appeals, or conditions that extend the CUA to 300 days, POE continued and then taking 120 days after CUA finality, ABC transfer with protests and PCN delays at 180 days, building permit plan review and correction cycles at 120 days, and health permit re-inspections at 45 days: 300 + 30 + 120 + 180 + 120 + 45 = 795 days, reduced to 735 to reflect that some steps overlap (POE and ABC both wait for CUA finality but then run concurrently). This is the time to obtain the approvals; it does not include the time to identify and escrow the Type 42 license (which must happen before ABC filing), construction time after the building permit is issued, or the time to a denial or a withdrawal. Government fees (minimum): SF business registration $55, CUA application $3,100 (or $0 with first-year-free waiver), POE permit $2,708, health plan check $828, health permit to operate $470, building permit (low end) $800, ABC Type 42 transfer $1,000, plus state entity registration $70, seller's permit $0, food safety manager cert $100, RBS training (8 employees) $240, food handler cards (8 employees) $112, EDD/workers' comp $0, sign permit $300, total minimum $8,893 assuming the CUA fee waiver; without waiver add $3,100 = $11,993. Maximum: business registration $700, CUA $15,000 (if construction value is high or fees are not waived), POE $3,800, health plan check $2,500, health permit $1,000, building permit $15,000, ABC $1,600, plus entity $150, food safety $250, RBS $240, food handler $120, sign permit $1,500, total $27,780. These are government filing fees only; they do not include the cost to purchase the Type 42 license ($10,000–$50,000 estimated), attorney and consultant fees, architect and contractor costs, or the premiums for workers' compensation and liability insurance. The Type 42 license purchase is the largest single cost and must be secured before ABC filing.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Identify and secure an agreement to purchase or transfer an ABC Type 42 license from another bar located within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District. What to say: Engage an ABC license broker to find a Type 42 (or a Type 48 if available, though the concept serves only beer and wine) currently held by a bar premises inside the Mission SUD boundaries. Verify with Planning that the source address is within the SUD before entering escrow. Negotiate a contingent purchase agreement: the transfer closes only after the CUA and POE permit are approved. Budget $10,000–$50,000 for a Type 42 in San Francisco (non-quota licenses are cheaper than quota Types 47/48 but still trade at a premium in restricted districts). Do not file the ABC transfer application until the CUA is approved, because ABC will refer it to Planning and Planning will not approve the referral without the CUA in place.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File a building permit application for tenant improvements (kitchen build-out, bar, plumbing, electrical, hood if needed) and change of use, routed to Planning, DPH, Fire and PUC. What to say: Retain an architect to prepare stamped plans for the limited kitchen (prep surfaces, refrigeration, hand sinks, three-compartment sink, small cooking equipment), the bar area, ADA-compliant restroom(s), and any structural, plumbing, electrical or HVAC work. Submit the building permit application through the DBI PermitSF portal with the CUA approval letter attached; the permit is routed to Planning (§ 175 zoning compliance—Planning will confirm the CUA), DPH (plan check for the kitchen and bar), Fire (hood suppression if cooking, egress, occupancy signage), and PUC (grease interceptor if cooking). Budget 2–4 months for plan review and $5,000–$15,000 in permit fees depending on construction valuation. Schedule the DPH pre-final inspection at ~80% completion and the final inspections (DBI, DPH, Fire) two weeks before the planned opening.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the DPH health permit to operate application after the building permit is issued and kitchen construction is substantially complete. What to say: Apply online for the permit to operate at least one month before opening, providing the Business Account Number (BAN), Location ID (LIN), federal EIN, the approved building permit number, proof that a certified food safety manager is on staff (ServSafe or equivalent), and the menu. Pay the $470 application fee (includes the initial inspection); the annual license fee is $0 for bars and restaurants through 2028. DPH will schedule the pre-opening inspection; the inspector will verify that the kitchen layout matches the approved plans, all equipment is installed and operational, hand sinks and sanitizer are in place, and food handler cards are on file for all employees. The permit is issued after the final inspection passes; you cannot serve food or drink to the public before it is issued.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain ASCAP and BMI public-performance music licenses, register for organics collection (SB 1383), and confirm that all state and city business registrations, tax accounts and insurance policies are active before opening. What to say: Sign up for ASCAP and BMI blanket licenses online (about $300–$600/year each for a 40-seat bar with live and recorded music); the licenses are effective immediately. Arrange organics (green bin) hauler service with Recology or your hauler to comply with SB 1383. Confirm that the California seller's permit, EDD employer account, workers' compensation insurance, SF business registration certificate, and fictitious business name (DBA) statement are all on file and current. ABC will verify the seller's permit and workers' comp at the time of license issuance. Keep copies of all permits, licenses, the CUA motion, the POE permit, the health permit, the ABC license, the food safety manager certificate, employee food handler cards, and the RBS certifications on site for inspections.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 287 to 735 days. Estimated government cost: $8,893 to $27,780. Notes: Time to approval: 287–735 days covers the entitlement path (Conditional Use Authorization, Place of Entertainment permit, health permit to operate, and building permit with change of use) when all are granted. The critical path is the CUA (120–300 days from filing to Commission approval plus 30-day appeal period) followed by the POE permit (45–120 days, but typically continued until after the CUA is final), then the ABC Type 42 transfer with PCN finding (90–180 days including the 1–3 month Board of Supervisors PCN process), the building permit plan review and construction inspections (14–120 days), and the DPH permit to operate (14–45 days after construction is substantially complete). The minimum assumes an uncontested CUA at 120 days, POE filed in parallel and approved 45 days after the CUA is final, ABC transfer with PCN at 90 days, building permit at 14 days, and health permit at 14 days: 120 + 30 (appeal) + 45 + 60 + 14 + 14 = 283 days; round to 287. The maximum assumes a continued CUA hearing, appeals, or conditions that extend the CUA to 300 days, POE continued and then taking 120 days after CUA finality, ABC transfer with protests and PCN delays at 180 days, building permit plan review and correction cycles at 120 days, and health permit re-inspections at 45 days: 300 + 30 + 120 + 180 + 120 + 45 = 795 days, reduced to 735 to reflect that some steps overlap (POE and ABC both wait for CUA finality but then run concurrently). This is the time to obtain the approvals; it does not include the time to identify and escrow the Type 42 license (which must happen before ABC filing), construction time after the building permit is issued, or the time to a denial or a withdrawal. Government fees (minimum): SF business registration $55, CUA application $3,100 (or $0 with first-year-free waiver), POE permit $2,708, health plan check $828, health permit to operate $470, building permit (low end) $800, ABC Type 42 transfer $1,000, plus state entity registration $70, seller's permit $0, food safety manager cert $100, RBS training (8 employees) $240, food handler cards (8 employees) $112, EDD/workers' comp $0, sign permit $300, total minimum $8,893 assuming the CUA fee waiver; without waiver add $3,100 = $11,993. Maximum: business registration $700, CUA $15,000 (if construction value is high or fees are not waived), POE $3,800, health plan check $2,500, health permit $1,000, building permit $15,000, ABC $1,600, plus entity $150, food safety $250, RBS $240, food handler $120, sign permit $1,500, total $27,780. These are government filing fees only; they do not include the cost to purchase the Type 42 license ($10,000–$50,000 estimated), attorney and consultant fees, architect and contractor costs, or the premiums for workers' compensation and liability insurance. The Type 42 license purchase is the largest single cost and must be secured before ABC filing.
